correctness.rationale: The seven degree-one components are intrinsically preserved by every projective automorphism of C=V(LQ). Their 21 pairwise intersections give five triple points and six doubles; the unique two collinear triples through P0 force P0 fixed and preserve or swap x=0,y=0. Fixing them individually and the third line x-y=0 gives matrices [x:y:cx+dy+ez]; target-pair constraints give exactly (c,d,e)=(0,0,1) or (2,1,-1). Swapping x,y would require simultaneously e=±2 and e=±1/2, impossible. The second matrix tau squares to identity, permutes all seven lines and fixes Q=z(z-2x-y)+(1-i)xy. These exhaustive two candidate line symmetries each fix Q and Qbar separately; coefficients of xy 1±i show Q and Qbar are nonproportional, so C and conjugate Cbar are not projectively equivalent. Field-of-moduli conclusion is restricted to projective equivalence over Qbar and Q(i). Independent exact SymPy incidence and polynomial-substitution checks reproduced five triple points, six doubles, invariance L/Q, plus coordinate-case arithmetic; no finite sampling claims completeness of PGL3.
residual_risks: Claim does not prohibit unrelated real nearly-free witnesses sharing the weak combinatorics; only same embedded curve and projectivities. Previous near-freeness is cited, not independently reproved from Jacobian syzygies.
